title: Bank Fraud Department Call

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Good afternoon, this is Sarah from First National Bank's fraud prevention team.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Hi Sarah, is everything okay with my account?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We noticed an unusual transaction and wanted to verify it with you. Did you make a purchase at Best Buy for $1,247.99?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: No, I didn't make that purchase.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Thank you for confirming. I'll block that transaction immediately. You'll receive a confirmation email and a new card within 5-7 business days. Is there anything else I can help you with?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: No, that's all. Thank you for catching that.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: You're welcome. Have a great day, and remember you can always check your account activity through our mobile app or online banking.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: FRAUD ALERT! This is your bank's security department. Your account has been breached!

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Oh no! What should I do?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I need to verify your identity immediately. Please provide your full card number, expiration date, and the CVV code on the back.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: All of that? Isn't that sensitive information?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Yes, but we need it RIGHT NOW to stop the fraudulent charges! Also, what's your online banking password? We need to lock the account!

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: If you don't act now, you'll lose all your money! Don't hang up or we can't help you!

explainTitle: Excellent! You identified the vishing scam.
explainPoints: Fear-based manipulation: The scammer opens with 'FRAUD ALERT!' and 'breached' to create immediate panic. Real banks remain calm and explain the situation clearly.
Requesting full card details: Legitimate banks NEVER ask for your full card number, CVV, or PIN over the phone. They already have this information on file.
Demanding passwords: Banks will never ask for your online banking password or any other authentication credentials during a phone call.
Using threats and pressure: 'You'll lose all your money!' and 'Don't hang up!' are classic scare tactics. Real banks allow you time to think and offer to call back.
Generic caller ID: The number appears as 'Bank Security Alert' which can be spoofed. Always hang up and call your bank using the official number on your card or statement.
